data.gender_notes: Sigismund is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements sigis, meaning victory, and mund, meaning mind or protection. Sigismund was a popular name among medieval European rulers and saints. In the Christian tradition, it symbolizes the triumph of faith and the protection of God. The name Sigismund carries the meaning “Victory of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sigismund usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of divine protection and victory.
data.etymology: Sigismund belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sigismund total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.name: Sigismund
in_english.meaning: king of peace, sign of peace, victory and peace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sigismund is derived from the Hebrew words סיבל (יסיל ארִי) and וריל (אייב עבר). It is associated with the concept of אייי שליו (ביור שוול אייב אייי) and has its roots in the biblical concept of עבר אתשה (ובייל, אייי שליו).

data.cultural_impact: Sigismund was the name of several kings and rulers in medieval Europe. One notable figure was Sigismund of Luxembourg, who was King of Hungary and Bohemia and played an instrumental role in the election of Friedrich III as Holy Roman Emperor. Another significant Sigismund was Sigismund I the Old, who was the first monarch of the House of Jagiellon in Poland and reigned from 1506 to 1548. The name has a rich historical context, evoking images of powerful and influential leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Sigismund is also associated with several saints. Saint Sigismund of Burgundy was a 6th-century Frankish prince who reigned over Burgundy and is venerated as a patron saint against the plague and as a protector of children. Saint Sigismund of Anhalt was a 12th-century duke of Anhalt and is remembered for his humility, charity, and dedication to the poor and the sick. The name Sigismund brings to mind the triumph of faith and the protecting presence of God in one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: As a name associated with Saint Saint Sigismund, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue.
